title: From Independent Sponsor to Committed Fund
summary: Explains the trade between raising equity for each acquisition and accepting pooled LP commitments, including a pledge-fund bridge and the operating duties of a fund manager.
confidence: high for the guide's stated framework; market terms are source estimates

notes.statement: Deal-by-deal sponsors assemble equity for each transaction and may receive transaction, company-management and profit-participation economics.
A pledge arrangement can speed repeat investor decisions while leaving each investment elective, so closing capital remains uncertain.
A committed fund exchanges per-deal investor choice for a defined strategy, portfolio-wide economics and ongoing manager obligations.
Sey's investor-fit and platform discussions describe buyer fundraising; this guide adds the LP's blind-pool and manager-capacity questions.

title: How to Start a Private Credit Fund
summary: Introduces the LP-funded lender's portfolio, income, fee, underwriting, loss, valuation and liquidity obligations.
confidence: high for conceptual descriptions; stated terms are time-sensitive source ranges

notes.statement: LP capital funds a portfolio of loans; the manager must originate, service, value and, when needed, work out those loans.
Interest distributions and losses make fee basis, concentration, leverage and recovery history material to LP outcomes.
The fund guide explains an industry model; it supplies no evidence that a prospective lender in Sey's collection completed a facility.

title: How to Start a Direct Lending Fund
summary: Examines loans to operating companies from the lender's side: origination, cash-flow underwriting, senior security, covenants, unitranche and workouts.
confidence: high for conceptual descriptions; terms and target markets vary

notes.statement: Direct lenders in the guide lend to operating businesses and emphasize sustainable cash generation, coverage, leverage and enterprise value in underwriting.
Sponsor-backed and founder-owned borrowers create different sourcing, diligence and workout responsibilities for the lender.
Unitranche can present one borrower facility while allocating different risk internally; it is not automatically senior to a separate mezzanine tranche in every deal.
Sey's bank process centers borrower approval and cash needs; the guide adds the lender's credit box, monitoring and restructuring capability.

title: How to Start a Mezzanine Fund
summary: Explains subordinated acquisition debt, the mix of cash and accrued interest, possible equity upside, intercreditor rights and reliance on exits or refinancing.
confidence: high for conceptual descriptions; stated terms are contextual, not universal

notes.statement: Mezzanine debt ranks behind senior debt and ahead of common equity in the described buyout structures.
Cash interest, capitalized interest and possible warrants create different cash and realization profiles.
Intercreditor payment blocks, standstills and cure rights can determine what the junior lender can do in distress.
Sey's documented bank-senior seller-debt example establishes ranking, while this guide explains a distinct institutional mezzanine product; the two should not be equated.
